loosened.reason: stablehand#25: both survivors change nothing a test can observe: SA_SIGINFO and SA_RESTART are distinct bits (| and ^ equal), and hold_signals only closes the microseconds between spawn and the child's pid being stored, a window no test can hit deterministically

kept.reason: read: no assertion maps — kimi's test checks kimi's Bearer header on a different engine and curl stand-in; this one checks dsh's x-dsh-auth-token header, a refused portable grant held until --token-command is given again, and a bound dsh home without a grant failing with its DSH_HOME fix. Merging across engines would hide which reader failed.

Setups conflict with a_setup_token_refused_usage_is_read_by_one_small_turn_and_its_usage_not_asked_again: that test's scope fault, refused claude and removed claude binary persist in its Books, and its counts of oauth/usage (1) and quota turns (2) would change if the 429/5xx/403/unreachable fallback cases were folded before it; none of the fallback assertions (each fault falls back, usage asked first again, both failing names the 429) are in it.

kept_files.reason: main.rs is the manual's home and the effect edge, not a shallow module: of its 482 prod lines ~290 are the clap tree's doc comments (the help, written with agent-help where each command's fact lives) and ~160 its argument definitions; the rest is one dispatch in which each command calls one module that decides it (usage, scan, login, command, order, run, statusline), with only the refusals and the store, clock and env reads of the register commands left here, as the agent-cli effect layer keeps them. Its churn is each new or changed command's help and flags; the deciding code has already moved out (command::parse, order::parse gather their own faults). Splitting the tree into another file would move that churn, not deepen anything; moving off, on, add and edit into account.rs would put effects into a pure module.

store.rs is already deep: one Store whose 18 methods (get, list, insert, put, put_booking, fill_hashes, remove, order/set_order, commands/set_commands, book, entries, start/end_session, sessions, reading_lock, open) each speak the domain (Account, Entry, Rank, Engine) and are all called from main, scan, run, usage or statusline, while it hides the SQL, the schema, the hash-checked migration (refusing another build's steps) and the 0700/0600 file guard. No pass-through or shallow wrapper: put and insert share one private write, the one-row JSON tables share one/set_one. Its churn is the append-only MIGRATIONS list and one table per feature (order, commands, sessions, organization), which is where a new stored fact belongs; splitting tables into files would spread one concept, the store, over several shallow modules. Its tests stay behind the interface except one trigger injected through conn to fail a booking, an in-module test.

kept_spans.reason: The hostname -s fallback of this_machine, the default machine name whenever $STABLEHAND_MACHINE is unset: what it decides is the real host program's answer, so only a test spawning the real hostname could assert it; tests set STABLEHAND_MACHINE to be host-independent.
